privateAddressWarning.title: Open sign-up without the private-address guard
privateAddressWarning.description: Anyone can create an account, and every member can create monitors and notification channels. Those connect from the worker, which can reach private, loopback and container-network addresses. Set MONITOR_DENY_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES=true (with MONITOR_ALLOW_CIDRS for subnets you do want to monitor) or turn sign-up off. See the hardening checklist in docs/Security.md.

hero.title: Know it’s down before your users do.
hero.description: Marmot watches your websites, APIs and servers, alerts the right people the moment something breaks and keeps your customers informed with public status pages.

features.title: Everything Uptime Kuma does, built for a team
features.description: The monitors and notifications you already know, with organizations, roles and an API on top.

monitorTypes.title: 30+ monitor types
monitorTypes.body: HTTP and keywords, TCP, ping, DNS, Docker, databases, MQTT, gRPC, push heartbeats and more.

notifications.title: 40+ notification providers
notifications.body: Slack, Discord, Teams, email, ntfy, webhooks and the rest of the Uptime Kuma catalogue.

statusPages.title: Public status pages
statusPages.body: Branded pages on your own domain with incidents, RSS and per-group uptime.

maintenance.title: Maintenance windows
maintenance.body: Schedule one-off or recurring windows so planned work never pages anyone.

organizations.title: Organizations and roles
organizations.body: Invite your team, separate environments by organization and control who can change what.

live.title: Live by default
live.body: Heartbeats stream to the dashboard as they happen; no refresh button, no polling.

selfHost.title: Open source. Self-host it any time.
selfHost.description: Marmot is AGPL-3.0 software. Run the same image on your own server with Postgres or MongoDB and Redis, and keep every check and every heartbeat on infrastructure you control.
